questions.question: Interpret the placement of analogous colors in a color wheel.
questions.solution_html:
• Ans
  • • SPACE
  • Space is the distance or area around, above, below, between, or within elements in a
  • design. It can be both positive and negative, and is used to create depth, balance
  • emphasis, and visual interest.
  • Positive Space :- Positive space refers to the subject or area within the design.
  • Negative Space :- Negative space is the background or the area that surrounds the design.
  • • SHAPE
  • Shape is the area or outline enclosed by lines. Shape is considered to be a 2 dimensional
  • element, While 3D elements have volume and mass. Therefore a painting has shape, a
  • sculpture has volume and mass.
  • When space is added to a simple shape, it begins to transform from a flat, two
  • dimensional form into a three-dimensional one. This introduction of space creates the
  • illusion of depth, making the design appear more realistic and engaging. Instead of looking
  • flat on the page, the form now seems to project outward or recede inward, giving it
  • volume, dimension, and a stronger visual presence. This use of space enhances the overall
  • design by making it more dynamic and expressive.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: design by making it more dynamic and expressive.
